examples.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ | $\dfrac{1}{9}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\dfrac{1}{18}$ | $\dfrac{1}{18}$ | $\dfrac{1}{6}$ |
| $X=3$ | $\dfrac{1}{9}$ | $\dfrac{1}{9}$ | $\dfrac{1}{18}$ |

Compute $f_{X|Y}(2 \,|\, 2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
examples.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function $f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
f_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) = P(X = x \,|\, Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
f_{X|Y}(2 \,|\, 2) = P(X = 2 \,|\, Y = 2).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X = 2 \,|\, Y = 2) = \dfrac{P(X = 2, Y = 2)}{P(Y = 2)} = \dfrac{f(2,2)}{f_Y(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(2) & =f(1,2)+f(2,2)+f(3,2) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{18} \\  & =\frac{7}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(2,2) = \dfrac{1}{6}.$ 

Finally, substituting  $f_Y(2) = \dfrac{7}{18}$ and $f(2,2) = \dfrac{1}{6}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(2\,|\,2) & =P(X=2\,|\,Y=2) \\  & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{6})}{(\frac{7}{18})} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.2$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $X=1$ | $0$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.25$ | $0.05$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0.15$ |

Compute $P(0\le Y\le 1\,|\,X=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
feedback.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le Y\le 1\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{P((0\le Y\le 1),X=3)}{P(X=3)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=3,(0\le Y\le 1))}{P(X=3)} \\  & =\frac{P(X=3,Y=0)+P(X=3,Y=1)}{P(X=3)} \\  & =\frac{f(3,0)+f(3,1)}{{f}_{X}(3)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(3) & =f(3,0)+f(3,1)+f(3,2) \\  & =0.1+0+0.15 \\  & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(3,0)=0.1$ and $f(3,1)=0.$ 

Finally, substituting our values into our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0\le Y\le 1\,|\,X=3) & =\frac{f(3,0)+f(3,1)}{{f}_{X}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.1+0}{0.25} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.25} \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
